title: Star-forming region NGC 346
caption: The star-forming region NGC 346, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 346, Small Magellanic Cloud · constellation Tucana · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Wispy gas surrounds a star cluster like a cobweb in this view of NGC 346, the brightest star-forming region in the Small Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring galaxy some 210,000 light-years from Earth. Found in Tucana (the Toucan), it measures approximately 200 light-years across.
The cobweb has a clear cause. Light, wind and heat from the cluster's massive stars have pushed and scattered the glowing gas in and around it, sculpting the delicate nebula that surrounds the stars.

Pictures like this help astronomers chronicle how stars are born and evolve, and show how that development changes the look of the surroundings over time. The image was obtained with the Wide Field Imager on the 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope at La Silla in Chile, and its field of view is about 30 arcminutes wide.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (30.53 x 30.53 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 1,800 × 1,800 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This enhanced-color visible-light image combines B, V and R broadband filters with a narrowband hydrogen-alpha filter, which is shown in blue. The mapping for the other filters is not published.
understand.eye: The hydrogen glow, which the eye would see as red, is shown in blue, and long exposures reveal faint gas an eye would miss.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: A star cluster surrounded by wispy, cobweb-like glowing gas.
